unlisted_practices: Build institutional readiness and governance capacity to scrutinize, regulate, and monitor rapidly evolving AI tools in disaster-prone settings.
Ensure AI and digital health tools rely on representative, context-sensitive data rather than partial realities.
Ensure communities have sustained influence over AI and digital innovation design and decision-making rather than time-limited consultation.
Design governance and learning arrangements that keep pace with evolving AI and make trade-offs explicit.
Ensure technological change redistributes decision-making authority and operational capacity to frontline teams, district managers, and communities rather than recentralizing it.
Build decision-makers' skills and confidence to assess the quality, bias, and relevance of datasets underlying digital and AI tools.

screen.reason: This is a commentary drawing on insights from the 8th Global Symposium on Health Systems Research (HSR2024), discussing governance, ethical safeguards, and recommendations for deploying digital technologies and AI in disaster-prone health systems.
